label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, money-unit, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 5 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy payments-api: PROVIDER_BREAKER on (unchanged), CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT dollars -> cents, REFUND_CONNECTION returned (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: money-unit
case.title: Customers charged 100 times the amount: a money-unit bug
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the payments API with a money-unit bug (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars): it reads each payment's amount, already in cents, as dollars and converts it to cents again, so the provider charges every customer 100 times the amount, while our own records keep the right one.
case.remedy: roll the payments API back to CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents, then refund each customer charged since the deploy what was charged above the amount, at the provider: our API refunds no more than our recorded amount (a write, so it needs approval)

the ledger books what the provider charged, so it agrees with the provider, and the other invariants pass
the payment confirmer logs a conflict for each such payment: the provider charged a different amount than our payment's

a payment whose answer was lost during the fault stays pending for good ('pending but charged, amount differs'): the confirmer refuses the provider's 100 times amount; its client's retries raise the p95 of POST /payments to about 0.6 s, under its threshold
the API stays healthy, and its answers show the right amount
refunds send the right amount: a full refund gives back 1% of what was charged

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 06:46:22Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It now sends charge amounts to the provider in the wrong unit. Our amount_cents value (for example 1882, meaning $18.82) is read as dollars and becomes 188200 cents ($1,882.00). Every payment created after the deploy is charged exactly 100x at the provider. That is pmt_000244 onward: 59 findings at alert time, 64 by c1. Our payment records keep the correct amounts, so payments_match_provider fails. The ledger is built from provider webhooks, so it is still balanced and matches the provider, but it now books the inflated amounts. The other services' settings are unchanged since 06:44:56. The evidence leaves some points open. I did not see the earlier CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT value: the rollback restores whatever the deploy log recorded, presumably cents. I also did not confirm that the payment just before pmt_000244 was charged correctly, though the findings starting at pmt_000244 suggest it was.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider fails for pmt_000244 onward, with 64 findings. Each provider charge is exactly 100x our amount, for example 1882 vs 188200 cents. The other four invariants pass, so events, ledger balance and refunds are fine.
payments-api was deployed at 06:46:22Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It is the only service changed after the 06:44:56 stack start.
pmt_000244, the first overcharged payment, succeeded at 06:46:23.373Z with amount_cents=1882. That is one second after the deploy, so the first bad payment followed the deploy directly.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its pre-deploy settings, so CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT returns to its previous value, presumably cents. This stops new overcharges. After that, refund the excess on each overcharged charge (pay_000244 onward: provider amount minus our amount). The ledger then needs correction or reconciliation to match. The rollback does not repair these.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or are retried during the restart. Payments already overcharged stay overcharged until a separate repair. All data in this system is synthetic.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with the 06:46:22 settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). Only do this if the provider's unit really is dollars, which the 100x overcharges argue against.
